result.summary: Adds an optional `delay_for` parameter to the `sendrawtransaction` RPC to postpone broadcasting transactions submitted via private broadcast. Delayed transactions are queued in memory with added randomized jitter (between 5 minutes and 50% of the requested delay, up to a 12-hour cap) and released by a periodic scheduler task after re-validating against the mempool.
result.problem: Immediate broadcast allows network observers to correlate transaction submission timing with off-chain user activity or specific events. Users currently have no built-in way to schedule or jitter private transaction announcements without using external cron jobs or custom scripts.
evidence: PR description: 'The aim is increased privacy, by making time-correlation-based tracking more difficult. This fits together with private broadcast: private connection broadcast tries to hide the originator node; randomized delay tries to hide the creation time.' (author claim, uncorroborated by linked issues)
result.scope_notes: Pending delayed transactions are held only in memory and are lost on node restarts or crashes.
result.changed_since_previous: No substantial design changes; rebased with minor refactors and tests retained.
result.card: This PR adds an optional delay_for parameter to sendrawtransaction to delay private broadcast by a requested duration plus randomized jitter. Delayed transactions are stored in-memory and re-evaluated with test-accept validation against the mempool before outbound Tor or I2P connections are opened. All motivation comes from author claims regarding time-correlation privacy without linked issues. Pending transactions are not persisted across node restarts.

risk.why: Bugs in release scheduling or delayed mempool validation could prevent transactions from broadcasting or unexpectedly drop user payments.
